items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: my biggest teacher was Leonard Heywood... he was my mentor.

ctx.x: Who were the teachers that you would credit?
Well my biggest teacher was Leonard Heywood. That was my first teacher and he was my music teacher, my drum teacher, he was the band director for the school, and my mentor.

items.title: Bernard Purdie interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: The interviewee discusses Leonard Heywood, correcting the interviewer's mention of 'Haven'. There is no mention of a person named Haven in the interviewee's response or narrative.

ctx.x: Well my biggest teacher was Leonard Heywood. That was my first teacher and he was my music teacher, my drum teacher, he was the band director for the school, and my mentor.

Heywood. Leonard Heywood. When I lost him, he moved to — well his wife said — moved to Phoenix, Arizona, for his health. Well I have no idea if that was true or not. As far as I’m concerned it was. Because she said it. But as time and the years go by it makes you wonder. Did they split up? He was an alcoholic, but of course I didn’t know what that was. They said he had a breathing problem. Okay, Arizona was the dry place. I mean I had the whole spiel. It was all given to me. And I believed it. Totally believed…
